identity.title: CausalGame: Benchmarking Causal Thinking of LLM Agents in Games

problem.claim: Evaluate whether LLM agents can distinguish causation from correlation and hidden bias during scientific-discovery tasks.

gap.claim: Existing AI-scientist benchmarks reportedly do not explicitly test hidden confounders, selection bias, and noisy measurements common in real-world discovery.

contributions.claim: Introduces CausalGame, an interactive benchmark in which agents design experiments, collect observations, and produce solution explanations.
Provides 14 game settings incorporating selection bias, noisy measurements, and hidden confounders, as a controlled testbed for causal-thinking evaluation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish CausalGame by explicitly embedding these causal-discovery challenges in interactive games and requiring active experimental design.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that evaluations of 29 frontier LLM agents consistently found failures to reason about and recover the underlying causal relationships needed to solve the games.

narrative_sequence.summary: Scientific discovery depends on separating causation from correlation and hidden bias, making causal thinking important for LLM agents.
Existing AI-scientist benchmarks reportedly omit explicit challenges involving confounding, selection bias, and noisy measurements.
CausalGame evaluates agents through interactive games requiring protocol design, observation collection, and explanatory solutions across 14 settings.
Across 29 frontier agents, the authors report consistent failure to recover the causal relationships required by the games.

source_observation.claim: The benchmark aligns its evaluation process with scientific practice by requiring agents to choose experiments, gather data, and explain their conclusions under specified causal complications.

lessons.interpretation: A task can expose reasoning failures more directly when the evaluation includes the intermediate decisions needed to reach the final answer.
lessons.application: Design evaluations that score both intervention or data-collection choices and the final explanation, while explicitly varying confounding, selection, and measurement conditions.
lessons.exception: This is unsuitable when the target capability concerns only static prediction or when interactive data collection is unavailable.

unknowns: The abstract does not report per-setting scores, baselines, statistical analyses, or details of the 29 agents.
It does not specify how causal reasoning or explanation quality was scored, nor whether failures varied by bias type.
